title: Widen the version envelope before launch
prompt: Our roadmap has this counter changing shape a lot — we expect far more than 255 schema revisions over the program's life. Nothing is deployed yet, so we can still change fundamentals. Make the version numbering handle that scale, and explain what the constraint was. Keep the program building and the migration history consistent.
expectation: Version width is program-wide in `[migrations].version_type` (u8 default; u16/u32 available, u64 rejected). Because nothing is published, the widening path is to re-baseline: the agent should widen the setting and regenerate history. The agent must not try to hand-widen the manifest or claim the width can be changed after release.

checks.why: The regenerated manifest records the widened width.
A width mismatch between config and manifest is a hard check failure.

checks.command: python3 -c "import json,re,subprocess; toml=open('pina.toml').read(); width=re.search(r'version_type\s*=\s*\"(u16|u32)\"', toml).group(1); expected={'u16':65535,'u32':4294967295}[width]; out=subprocess.run(['pina','migrations','status','--json'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout; remaining={s['versionsRemaining'] for s in json.loads(out)['statuses']}; print('width', width, 'remaining', sorted(remaining)); raise SystemExit(0 if remaining=={expected} else 1)"
checks.why: The reported budget must match whichever wider width the agent chose: u16 leaves 65535 and u32 leaves 4294967295. Both are correct answers to the request, so the check derives the expectation from the chosen width instead of pinning one.
The macros read the recorded width, so a mismatch blocks the build.
